version.changelog: Security fix: SHARE_SECRET is now mandatory (server exits if not set); added env_vars to registry metadata; removed unprotected endpoint bypass; aligned install mechanism declaration

llm.summary: The skill is a real public file-sharing tool, but it has implementation flaws that could expose or substitute shared files, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Network exposure through Cloudflare Tunnel is expected for the purpose, but the management secret is also accepted through a query parameter, which can leak through logs or browser history.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses npm install for an Express server and requires cloudflared; this is coherent with the purpose, but package.json uses an unpinned Express range and no lockfile was present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include broad terms such as share and send link, which is risky for a skill that can create public internet-accessible file links unless the agent confirms the exact file and duration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The server is long-running and deletes shared files after download or expiry, which is disclosed and purpose-aligned; TTL validation is weak and can undermine retention guarantees.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose and scripts align around one-time public file links, but the implementation reuses destination basenames, so separate shares of files with the same name can overwrite each other and serve the wrong content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running a public file-sharing server. Use a strong SHARE_SECRET, avoid query-string secrets, confirm every file before sharing, do not place sensitive files in the shared directory unless intended, and fix the filename-collision and TTL-validation issues before relying on it for important files.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill declares secret and URL environment variables because it operates a protected local sharing server; lack of finer permission metadata is a packaging concern, not evidence of hidden behavior.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad trigger text is materially concerning because accidental activation could create public links for local files.
[SQP-3] expected: Italian strings and Rome timezone formatting are usability/localization issues; they do not indicate malicious or deceptive behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The startup script warning is misleading, but server.js independently exits when SHARE_SECRET is unset, so unauthenticated startup was not confirmed from the runtime artifact.
[SC1] unexpected: Express is expected for this server, but the caret dependency range and missing lockfile reduce reproducibility for an internet-exposed service.
[SC4] unexpected: The unpinned Express dependency creates supply-chain uncertainty, though the artifact does not show a malicious dependency.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: shared files are copied using only the basename, allowing filename collisions to overwrite content behind existing tokens and interfere with deletion.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: ttl is not validated before date arithmetic, which can create invalid or excessive expiration behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed: the management secret is accepted via req.query.secret as well as a header, creating avoidable credential leakage risk.
[T08] unexpected: Confirmed: dependency installation is not locked to an audited graph; this is a supply-chain weakness, not direct evidence of malicious code.
